Dressing Room
You call Pandey-ji at 3 AM. He drives to Pinky's school himself the next morning, and every morning after, in his slippers.
We have a car outside your sister's school. Plain clothes. She won't even know. You did the right thing. Now let us do ours.
Then the call that changes everything. The state selectors. Senior team. Ranji Trophy. Saturday.
The senior UP dressing room. Fifteen kit bags, two physios, one broken AC, and a corner nobody sits in.
That's my corner, kid. Fourteen years. 9,926 first-class runs. Zero India caps. Sit anywhere else.
This is my last season. Seventy-four runs from ten thousand. Then they can put my name on a bench somewhere and forget it.
"Teach me how to bat long."
His secrets make you a better batter tomorrow.
"Ten thousand. We'll get you there."
Make a promise.
Sit in his corner anyway.
Respect is taken, not given.
Hm. Sit. Watch the bowler's shoulders, not the ball. And never, ever trust a dressing room that agrees with everything.
Hahaha! Okay. Okay. You'll do. But you're carrying my kit bag for a week.
Friday night. A quiet man in a grey shirt is waiting in your hotel room. He is already sitting down.
Anti-Corruption Unit. We know Sunny met you in Kanpur. We know about an envelope. What we don't know is what you're going to tell me now.
Tell him everything.
Confess. Take what comes.
"I don't know any Sunny."
Lie. Hope the photo never surfaces.
Hm. Okay. Enjoy your debut.
Thank you. It won't make this go away. But it will be the only thing that matters when it's over.
Saturday morning. Awadh Times, front page. "THE PLOT THICKENS: A fire, a moneylender and a bus stand in Rajgarh." By Neha Sharma.
By lunch, Ramesh-ji is in a police jeep. By evening, the land sale is frozen pending inquiry. Papa calls you and cannot speak.
Day three of your Ranji debut. UP vs Mumbai. Last half hour of the day. Rocky is on 96. You're at the other end.
Six balls left in the day. Don't get out. Don't do anything stupid. I'll get my hundred tomorrow. Or I'll die trying.
The Last Over
Mumbai's quick, the new ball, fading light. Rocky is on 96 at the other end. Survive 6 balls.
STUMPS!
Rocky hugs you on the way off.
OUT
The tail is exposed. Rocky is stranded.
Next morning, Rocky Bhatia pulls the first ball for four. Hundred. Ten thousand first-class runs. He kneels on the pitch and doesn't get up for a whole minute.
Next morning, the last wicket falls in the first over. Rocky walks off on 98 not out. He never plays first-class cricket again.
In the dressing room he hands you his bat. "Get the runs I didn't."
Rohan Mehra. Sports agent. Big fan.
The PCL auction is in 10 days. You're on three franchise shortlists.
One of those franchises is part-owned by a man your friend Sunny works for.
The PCL auction is in ten days. And Sunny Bhai's boss owns part of one of the teams that wants you.
